claims.claim: Model weights, stage instructions, and decision rule remain fixed; the improvement library evolves across tasks.
claims.caveat: Do not describe training or algorithm self-rewriting.

claims.claim: Each new task starts at the common base execution harness H0; prior components are selectively reused through improvement.
claims.caveat: Execution harnesses are not automatically carried forward between tasks.

claims.claim: Parallel k controls one population update with k invariant candidates, k domain candidates, and k compositions.
claims.caveat: Width, not k serial generations; equal k is not equal compute across methods.

claims.claim: For k > 1 the selector chooses an existing anonymized output without synthesis; k=1 bypasses selection.
claims.caveat: Adoption is not verified optimality or correctness; base outputs are eligible.

claims.claim: One-step Harness2 improves the base metric in all twelve benchmark/configuration pairs.
claims.caveat: Two models x two initial harnesses x three benchmark metrics; not every competing baseline/domain is beaten.

claims.claim: The largest one-step WorkBuddy macro-average gain is 11.5 points for GLM-5/OpenCode: 64.2 to 75.7.
claims.caveat: Absolute points on an unweighted three-domain mean; not relative percent.

claims.claim: The largest one-step JobBench gain is 4.5 points for Gemini 3.5 Flash/OpenCode: 31.5 to 36.0.
claims.caveat: JobBench evaluates 34 held-out tasks with weighted rubric scoring.

claims.claim: The largest one-step LAB Partial gain is 11.8 percentage points for GLM-5/OpenCode: 59.6 to 71.4.
claims.caveat: Criterion pass rate, not fully solved task rate; total criterion denominator unspecified.

claims.claim: Gemini 3.5 Flash/Codex on LAB has Meta-Harness 76.5 versus one-step Harness2 75.6.
claims.caveat: A baseline exception; three-run means and SDs do not supply a significance test.

claims.claim: Removing the library/scoping/composition lowers WorkBuddy and JobBench scores in the tested k=1 Gemini/OpenCode ablation.
claims.caveat: Limited tested configuration; not an additive component decomposition.

claims.claim: Parallel k=5 increases main-table scores over k=1 by 2.9-3.9 WorkBuddy points, 3.0-4.2 JobBench points, and 2.6-6.7 LAB percentage points.
claims.caveat: WorkBuddy ranges refer to Avg., not individual domains. Rows are mean deltas; k=5 SDs absent.

claims.claim: A completed-library leave-one-out rerun changes WorkBuddy 77.5 to 79.4 and JobBench 36.0 to 37.7.
claims.caveat: Retrospective offline reuse includes later-task entries; repeated execution may contribute.

claims.claim: Post-improvement removal of skills reduces the WorkBuddy mean from 80.8 to 75.5; script removal gives 77.1; prompt-group removal gives 79.3.
claims.caveat: Gemini/OpenCode k=5; no reoptimization; effects not additive.

claims.claim: WorkBuddy tool-error rate falls from 0.8% to 0.5%; JobBench and LAB tool-call counts increase after refinement.
claims.caveat: WorkBuddy change is -0.3 percentage points or -37.5% relative; lower error rate is distinct from fewer calls.

claims.claim: The failure analysis includes selection of a 55-point output despite an available 95-point candidate.
claims.caveat: Retrospective evaluation scores were hidden from the selector; displayed reference is 96.

claims.claim: Main benchmark means and SDs are over three independently shuffled streams; WorkBuddy Avg. is a domain macro-average.
Executor #Steps counts model turns; Figure 6 separately includes execution and improvement token costs before submission.
claims.caveat: Fewer executor steps does not imply lower total pipeline compute or dollars.

claims.claim: Reflection examines rejected candidates too and may decline a durable lesson when evidence is insufficient.
claims.caveat: Single runs and multiple simultaneous edits can leave attribution confounded.

claims.claim: The reported results support bounded harness adaptation, not indefinite monotonic self-improvement or universal correctness.
claims.caveat: Guide synthesis; budgets and benchmarks are limited and feedback remains fallible.
